basics.name: Radin Hamidi Rad
basics.label: Postdoctoral Fellow, University of Toronto
basics.summary: Computational intelligence researcher working at the intersection of generative AI, information retrieval, natural language processing, and graph-based machine learning. My program develops agentic search and retrieval systems, robust and secure LLM-based methods, and explainable tools for evidence synthesis.

skills.name: AI and Language
keywords: Generative AI and large language models

skills.name: Search and Retrieval
keywords: Evidence synthesis and decision support systems

work.name: University of Toronto
work.summary: Building agentic retrieval and evidence-synthesis systems in collaboration with computing and health-research teams.

work.name: Mila – Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute
work.summary: Research on adversarial robustness in information retrieval, knowledge graphs, and LLM-based systems.
highlights: Postdoctoral fellow on the CAD 100,000 CAISI Catalyst Grant project Adversarial Robustness in Knowledge Graphs.

work.name: University of Toronto
work.summary: Developed agentic retrieval and evidence-synthesis systems; collaborated across computing and health-research teams; taught a graduate course and mentored graduate researchers.

work.name: Microsoft Research
work.summary: Developed neural NLP methods for interactive topic tagging and routing in community question-answering systems; the work was published at ECIR 2024.
highlights: Mentors: Silviu Cucerzan and Nirupama Chandrasekaran.

work.name: Vector Institute
work.summary: Developed and evaluated language-model pipelines for conversational question answering.

Thesis: Synchronizing Robot Arm With Human Arm Moves Using KINECT.

teaching.name: INF1343H: Data Modeling and Database Design
teaching.summary: Sessional Lecturer, Faculty of Information, University of Toronto. Graduate course, approximately 70 students.
highlights: Designed the syllabus, lectures, assignments, projects, and grading rubrics; delivered the course in person.

teaching.name: INF2204H: Digital Connectivity for Information Systems
teaching.summary: Sessional Lecturer, Faculty of Information, University of Toronto. Graduate course, approximately 25 students.
highlights: Designed and delivered course materials, including lectures and assignments, and provided student mentorship.

teaching.name: Teaching and Graduate Assistantships
teaching.summary: 23 teaching- and graduate-assistant appointments across Toronto Metropolitan University and Amirkabir University of Technology.
highlights: Subjects included data and information management, business intelligence and analytics, Big Data Analytics, operating systems, embedded systems, computer networks, and microprocessor systems.
Designed and organized laboratory materials for the Software Design and Architecture course at Toronto Metropolitan University.

projects.name: Agentic Deep Search and Iterative Retrieval
projects.summary: Agentic systems for complex question answering through iterative search, reading, and reasoning.
highlights: Question’s Gambit achieved 90.5% answer accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus, ranking first in recall (96.6%) and the only academic submission among the leaderboard’s leaders.
ADORE uses retrieval-grounded relevance feedback for query expansion and improved average nDCG@10 by 122.9% over BM25 on BRIGHT.

projects.name: Open Research Infrastructure for Agentic Retrieval
projects.summary: Open tools for building, reproducing, and evaluating retrieval pipelines.
highlights: Built and publicly released TRAWL, a visual platform for composing, testing, and evaluating agentic retrieval flows.
Co-developed QueryGym (The Web Conference Companion 2026), a toolkit for reproducible LLM-based query reformulation, and contributed to a SIGIR 2026 reproducibility study of reformulation methods.

projects.name: LLM Safety and Adversarial Robustness
projects.summary: Failure modes of aligned LLMs and retrieval systems through prompt-embedding optimization, adversarial content injection against neural rankers, graph poisoning, and adversarial edge perturbation.
highlights: Combines attacks, evaluation resources, and evidence for robust system design.

projects.name: WISEST: Human-Centred Evidence Synthesis
projects.summary: Led AI development for an internally deployed system that supports structured, explainable assessment of systematic reviews.
highlights: Collaboration between the University of Toronto, the University of British Columbia, and Unity Health Toronto; contributed to a peer-reviewed article in Research Synthesis Methods.

projects.name: Graph Representation Learning and Team Formation
projects.summary: Neural representations and retrieval methods for complete and incomplete heterogeneous graphs, with applications to subgraph search, expert-team formation, and recommendation.
highlights: Released research software including ROKSANA, PyTFL, and PyDHNet.
